title: Graph pane: [ ⇱ pane ] and middle-click open one graph as a pane pinned to its chat; per-run poll loops
operator_decision: 2026-10-08 (TRACK.md, USER GRAPH DESIGN): [ ⇱ pane ], and an aux-click or middle-click on a sub-tab, open that one graph as a PANE in the dwindle tiling beside the chat. The pane is PINNED to that chat and never follows focus. One graph per pane; split for more graph panes.
why:
The registry already has the seams: paneKinds (registry.js:12-15, 77-78, 84), host.openXPane (app.js:172-180, 1743-1756) and splitExtras (registry.js:16, app.js:828). Focus already behaves as the design wants:
- A click on an xpane focuses it (notes/pane.js:141).
- `inspected` stays on the last chat (app.js:103-105, 1732), so the inspector keeps that chat and a pinned pane is never retargeted.
The one blocker is runs.js: one loop and one `model` per page (runs.js:208, 357-388). watch() drops whatever loop is running, so a tab and a pane on two runs stop each other's polls.
what:
graph/pane.js (new). One import line in graph/index.js (`import './pane.js';`) registers it, as notes does from its index (notes/index.js:15). No app.js edit: every seam is in the registry.
- `paneKinds.add({ kind: 'graph', Pane: GraphPane, title, status, cwd })`.
- `splitExtras.add(graphItems)`.

Pane data, fixed at open (app.js:176 copies it onto the pane):
- `{ chat: <sid> | null, pick: 'turns' | <rid> | <chat-run key> }`, with GP-a's pickOk shapes. 'new' is never a pane.
- Never `s` (it goes stale) and never a chat pane's id (a pane's sid changes through showIn, app.js:207-223). The pane is pinned by sid.

`toPane(chat, pick, { at, dir } = {})`:
- It refuses, returning null without calling host:
  - 'new';
  - a pick that fails pickOk;
  - a chat that fails chatOk;
  - 'turns' with no chat.
- Dedupe: the key is `turns:<chat>` for turns, else the pick itself (a rid is the same run from any chat). An open graph pane with that key is focused with host.focusPane, as openNote does (notes/store.js:492-507).
- Otherwise: `host.openXPane('graph', { chat, pick }, { at: at ?? host.inspected()?.id, dir })`.
  - `at` is explicit because a click in the inspector does not move ui.focus. The default anchor (app.js:174) could split a focused terminal or graph pane instead of the chat.
  - With no dir given, the split follows dwindle (core/tile.js:17-27).

The strip (graph/strip.js, GP-a's file):
- Every sub-tab except [ new run ] sits in a span with:
  - `onMouseDown`: when button === 1, preventDefault (no autoscroll);
  - `onAuxClick`: when button === 1 only (auxclick also fires for the right button), preventDefault and toPane.
  This is app.js:1204-1207.
- The K's click: ctrl or meta opens the pane, otherwise it picks (app.js:1209).
- `[ ⇱ pane ]` comes after [ new run ] and opens the selected graph. It is off when 'new' or nothing is selected.
- The handlers are exported pure functions, so they can be tested. index.js passes `onPane = (pick) => toPane(sid, pick)`.

GraphPane({ p, rect, focused, act }):
- The frame: `<section class="pane frame gpane" style=${paneStyle(rect)} data-pane=${p.id} data-kind=${p.kind} tabindex="-1" onMouseDown=${() => act.focus(p.id)}>` (registry.js:13-14; notes/pane.js:140-141).
- An ftitle line `⋔ <chat label> · <graph label>`, as text.
- Glyphs (+ split, × close) copied from notes/pane.js:33-41. Do not import panes/session.js (node cannot load it; tests/README.md:3), and never call act.paneMenu (it is chat-only and reads p.s, app.js:886-900).
- The body is `<div class="scroll grun">` (term.css:171) and holds ONE graph:
  - Every render, `s = host.chatPanes().find((x) => x.sid === p.chat)?.s ?? null` (app.js:1750). Tiles redraws its xpanes whenever ui.panes changes (app.js:1479, 1506), so this stays current.
  - 'turns' with s: TurnGraph({ s, sid: p.chat }) (W3).
  - 'turns' with no s, one sentence by where the chat is:
    - not open here: '<label> is not open here' and `[ open it ]`, which calls host.openCmd('open ' + chat) (app.js:588-591, 1755). The person presses Enter.
    - in core/hub.js `trash`: '<label> is in the trash: restore it from the sidebar'.
    - in neither the list nor the trash (perch): 'this chat is gone'.
    - door: 'not open here'.
    The pane never builds a Session (sessionFor is private, app.js:115, and the 4-stream cap is counted from ui.panes, app.js:136-145). It never closes itself: closing from a 5 s poll would move the layout under the mouse.
  - A perch rid: RunView (view.js:236) with `m = R.modelFor(rid).value`.
    - `listed` is the row from runList or the chat cache.
    - onCancel and onAbandon are the tab's runs.js actions; Steps and ParkAsk are live, since it is the same run.
    - `notice=${R.noticeFor(R.notice.value, pick)}` (GP-a's rule and helper): a refusal of this run (a 503, a 409 not parked or child alive) is drawn in this pane under the run's status. Without it the pane's refusal would be silent, or drawn under whatever chat the tab shows (runs.js:420, 430, 440; index.js:38).
    - It works with the chat closed, because a perch run needs no Session.
    - A pruned run shows RunView's gone sentence.
  - A chat-run key: 'not drawn here yet'. GP-c fills it.
- `useEffect(() => (ridOk(pick) ? R.follow(pick) : undefined), [pick])`. The release is the cleanup.

title(p) and status(p):
- 'graph <chat label> · <pick label>', through clean. The chat label is label(row) from the hub list (hub.js:79), else the id, else 'no chat'. The pick label is 'turns', the rid, or the chat run's name.
- status adds the run's state.
- The status line draws them while the pane has focus (app.js:1638, 1657).

cwd(p): the pinned chat's folder. It is s.hello.peek().cwd, else the hub list row's cwd, else ''. host.cwd and `:term` use it (app.js:1736, 1752).

graphItems(p, dir), the split menu ("split for more graph panes"):
- For a chat pane (p.sid) or a graph pane (p.chat), one item: `{ label: 'graph', sub: [...] }`.
  - The sub holds 'turns', then that chat's runs, newest STRIP_RUNS (from GP-a's cache).
  - The menu is built synchronously when it opens (app.js:824-828), and GP-a's cache holds only chats the graph tab has shown or acted on. So for a chat with no cache entry, graphItems starts one loadChatRuns(chat) through the lane (hubPoll: a second open while it waits shares the request, lane.js:8-10), and the sub shows 'turns' plus a greyed `{ label: 'runs', off: "reading this chat's runs: open the menu again" }`. A chat read OK with no runs offers 'turns' alone.
  - A graph pane warms its chat's cache once when it mounts, if there is no entry, so splitting from it lists the runs.
  - Each entry calls toPane(chat, key, { at: p.id, dir }).
- For a graph pane with no chat: the newest runs from the unfiltered list.
- For any other kind: [].
- Under a door: turns only.
- Labels go through clean.

runs.js, per-run loops (the blocker):
- `follow(rid) -> release`:
  - one loop per rid, reference-counted;
  - the same pass(m, live), retryMs and pollMs rules (runs.js:45-51, 323-354);
  - a second follow adds a reference, never a second loop;
  - release is idempotent, and the last release stops the loop.
- `modelFor(rid)`: the signal of that rid's model, published by that rid's loop. For any ridOk rid it exists at once, holding null until a loop publishes, so a pane that reads it in its first render (Preact runs the follow effect after that render) draws RunView's 'reading the run…' and never throws. A rid that fails ridOk gives null; the pane checks ridOk before reading it. These entries are capped like modelOf's (runs.js:306-315), and a followed rid is never evicted.
- watch(rid), unwatch(), poke() and `model` keep their meaning for the tab, so runs.test.mjs:143-247 passes unchanged:
  - watch is the tab's one hold, taken through follow;
  - model mirrors the tab's rid.
- `poke(rid)` pokes that rid's loop; `poke()` pokes the tab's. answerRun, cancelRun and abandonRun poke their own rid (runs.js:418, 427, 437).
- modelOf's cap (runs.js:306-315) never evicts a followed rid.
- One module-level visibilitychange listener, held only while any loop lives. When the page comes back it pokes each loop once (a hidden page stops every loop, runs.js:373, so this poke is what restarts it). It is the ONLY visibility poke: openTab's `back` (runs.js:454) keeps refresh() and drops its poke(), or the tab's run would be read twice (a poke during a pass runs a second pass at once, runs.js:369, 376). A pane never calls openTab (it makes an interval per call, runs.js:451-457), and never reads or writes picks or `model`.
- resetRuns stops every loop.
- pass, live, loadHealth, loadRuns and refresh keep the text the source scan pins (runs.test.mjs:536-553).

steps.js (W2b-2's file, merged):
- `showAll` (steps.js:23) is keyed by rid, as `wide` is (steps.js:24). Unfolding one run's steps then never unfolds another run's in a pane.
- One run's fold state stays shared by every view of that run: one run, one fold. The keys `rid/…` in steps.js:24, park.js:13 and context.js:13 are unique across chats, because rids are.

Reload: no graph pane comes back. That is how chats and notes behave:
- xpanes start empty (app.js:60);
- boot reopens one chat pane (app.js:1795-1797);
- notes stash only unsaved text (notes/store.js:23, 278-299).
The strip's per-chat choice does come back (GP-a).

CSS: .gpane rules in graph.css, square edges.

Docs:
- graph/README.md rows for pane.js and the runs.js loop API;
- a tests/README.md row for pane.test.mjs.
owns_files: webui/term/graph/index.js (the pane.js import and the onPane prop)
webui/term/graph/runs.js (follow, modelFor, poke(rid), the loop table)
webui/term/graph/steps.js (showAll keyed by rid: one line and its use)
live_check:
Fake perch on PORT=48144, served from GP-b's worktree, with master's binaries after RT. The same FAKE_PERCH_ARGS as GP-a, FAKE_PERCH_BASE=$HOME/.cache/GP-b-live, and the case file starting at `b`. Browser-pane steps for the orchestrator:
1. Open chat A, then start r1 from A's strip. It parks.
2. Middle-click r1's sub-tab. A pane opens split from A's pane (not from whatever else had focus), and the status line names it.
3. Click inside the pane: the inspector still shows A.
4. Open chat B and focus it. The pane still shows r1 (pinned); the tab shows B.
5. Answer the park inside the pane. The run goes running, then done. Open the graph tab with no chat: r1 reads done there too, and no second poll loop runs for r1 (network panel: one runs/r1 request per second).
5b. A refusal in the pane: write `b` to the case file, start r2 from A's strip and middle-click it into a pane, then focus B. curl POST /hub/runs/r2/abandon (bearer from the 0600 header file), then within 5 s (the parked poll) pick option 0 and [ answer ] in the pane: the pane shows the perch's 409 sentence under r2's status, and the inspector tab (on B) shows nothing of it.
6. On A, [ ⇱ pane ] with [ turns ] selected opens A's turn graph as a second pane. Middle-click r1 again: the existing pane is focused, not doubled.
7. The split menu (+) on a graph pane of A offers 'graph ▸ turns, r2, r1'.
8. Close A's chat pane. The turns pane says A is not open here, and [ open it ] prefills `:open <A>`. The r1 pane still draws r1.
9. Trash A from the sidebar: the turns pane says it is in the trash. Restore A: it says not open here again.
10. Write `a` to the case file, start r3 from A and middle-click it into a pane. Close the graph tab (pick another inspector tab) while r3 is running in the pane: the pane keeps polling at 1 s.
11. Reload: the graph panes are gone, and A's sub-tab choice is kept. With the inspector on another tab, + on the chat pane the reload reopened offers 'graph ▸ turns' and a greyed 'runs' line; opened again, it lists that chat's runs.
12. The console is clean. Screenshots go to scratch. --stop.
risk: runs.js becomes a loop table. A bug there stops the tab's own run view, so the existing watch tests must pass unchanged. Load stays bounded: only one perch run can be running or parked at a time (runs.js:36-37, 164; the perch's 409), and an ended run stops polling (pollMs null, runs.js:45-48). Editing steps.js, W2b-2's file, needs W2b-2 merged first.
notes: Decided here, not by the user: a pinned pane stays when its chat closes or is trashed, and says so in one line; it never closes itself. One pane per graph (the notes rule, notes/store.js:494): a second open focuses the first. One run's fold state is shared by every view of that run.
Optional seams left out to keep it small: chatMenuItems 'graph beside' in the sidebar menus, and a `:graph` command (BASE_COMMANDS has none, app.js:556-575).
noticeFor(n, rid) and the notice's rid are GP-a's (runs.js); this slice only passes the pane's run to it.
